title: Top Space Heaters for Cold Rooms (2026)
summary: The Dr. Infrared DR-968 is the best all-round heater, the DREO 718 the best tower, and the DREO 320 the best cheap one.
method: Picks come from HGTV (20 heaters tested, updated Sept 16, 2026) and Bob Vila (13 heaters tested, Oct 2, 2026). The Dr. Infrared DR-968 and the Lasko bathroom heater appear in both; the DREO 718 is also backed by Family Handyman's tests.
assumptions: Prices change often, so we quote only figures the sources show. The DREO 320 and De'Longhi SlimStyle are each covered by one outlet, and the Lasko bathroom models differ by number (CD08200 vs CD08210). Consumer Reports' space heater ratings are paywalled, so they are not used.

products.name: Dr. Infrared Heater DR-968
why: Bob Vila's testers named the DR-968 their best overall space heater, loving its quiet hum, thermostat and timer. In a 156 sq ft room they felt a change within 15 minutes and a 10°F rise by 33 minutes. HGTV picks it as best for large rooms, noting infrared heat that spreads evenly without the housing getting very hot.
Family Handyman also lists a Dr. Infrared heater as its best infrared pick, so three outlets agree on it.
specs: 1,500W infrared heater in a wood cabinet, with remote
Thermostat and timer up to 12 hours (Bob Vila)
19 lb with built-in casters; three-year warranty (HGTV)
HGTV listed $113 (regular $125) at Amazon; check the current price
pros: Quiet, even heat with accurate thermostat
Casters make it easy to move
products.best_for: Living rooms and larger spaces where you want quiet, steady heat
products.skip_if: You want something light and compact for a desk or bathroom
products.amazon_listing: Dr Infrared Heater DR-968 Portable Space Heater, 1500-Watt, Cherry

products.name: DREO Tower Heat 718 Space Heater
why: HGTV's best overall out of 20 tested: easy controls and remote, powerful even heating, quiet, and a good fan. It has eight safety features, including tip-over and overheat protection.
Family Handyman also names the Dreo Solaris 718 its best overall and safest space heater, though HGTV calls its test model the Tower Heat 718, so confirm the listing.
specs: Five heat settings, remote included, oscillating tower
8 lb; rated for large rooms by HGTV
Safety: tip-over and overheat protection, cool-touch housing, child lock, flame-retardant materials
HGTV listed $130 at Amazon; check the current price
pros: Strong, even heat and a good fan
products.best_for: Bedrooms, offices and moderate rooms that need fast, quiet heat
products.skip_if: You want the cheapest option or an infrared heater

products.name: DREO Heater 320 Adjustable-Tilt
why: HGTV's best value pick: it looks and works like a premium heater and performed much like the pricier DREO 718 at half the cost. The adjustable tilt lets you aim heat where you want it.
Only HGTV covers this exact model in our sources.
specs: 3.5 lb; best for small to medium rooms
Same safety set as the 718: tip-over, overheat protection, child lock
HGTV listed $50 at Amazon ($41 at Walmart); check the current price
cons: Short height limits how far heat spreads
products.best_for: Small rooms, desks and bedrooms on a budget
products.skip_if: You need to heat a large open room
products.amazon_listing: DREO Space Heater 1500W, 60° Adjustable Tilt, Portable Heater for Office

products.name: Lasko Ceramic Bathroom Space Heater ALCI
why: Both HGTV (CD08200) and Bob Vila (CD08210) pick a Lasko ceramic heater with an ALCI safety plug for bathrooms. In Bob Vila's test the plug tripped when the heater was sprayed with water and worked again after drying.
One big button controls it. Neither outlet found automatic tip-over protection, so do not leave it where it can be knocked over.
specs: 3.35 lb, small rooms (HGTV); warmed a 156 sq ft room by 5°F in 20 minutes (Bob Vila)
HGTV lists a three-year warranty and $40 (regular $55) at Amazon; model numbers differ, so check the listing
products.best_for: Bathrooms, laundry rooms and other damp spots
products.skip_if: You need a heater for a living room or have pets or kids who might tip it
products.amazon_listing: Lasko 8" Ceramic Bathroom Space Heater - ALCI Safety Plug - White - CD08200 | 1500W, Timer

products.name: De'Longhi SlimStyle Digital Convection Panel Heater
why: Bob Vila picks the SlimStyle for basements because of an antifreeze mode that stays dormant and kicks on when the space drops to 45°F, using very little energy. Most heaters cannot be set below about 60°F.
It runs quietly, mounts on the floor or wall, and has tip-over and overheat protection plus eco mode and timers. Only Bob Vila covers it in our sources.
specs: 1,500W convection panel heater with four modes
Antifreeze mode switched on at 45°F in testing, not the 41°F the maker claims
Floor or wall mounting hardware included
Bob Vila's test price range for all heaters was $45 to $189; check the current price
pros: Digital display, eco mode and timers
cons: Antifreeze mode triggered a few degrees higher than advertised
products.best_for: Basements, garages and spaces that need freeze protection
products.skip_if: You want a remote or a fast-heating personal heater

tips.title: How to choose
items: Bob Vila says about 10 watts per square foot, so a 1,500W heater suits roughly a 15 x 10 ft room. HGTV found none of the big-room claims held up, so buy a bit stronger than you need and turn it down.
Look for tip-over and overheat protection; use ALCI plugs in damp rooms and keep 3 feet of clearance from fabric and furniture (HGTV, Bob Vila).
Bob Vila warns this raises fire risk; plug directly into the wall.
HGTV says space heaters are not meant to replace central heating and will raise your bill if used that way.

faq: Can I leave a space heater on overnight?
HGTV says most makers and the CPSC advise against it because of fire risk; warm the room first and turn it off before bed.
Infrared costs more but is quieter and more efficient, while ceramic is cheaper, louder and can dry the air (HGTV).
On a level, hard, non-flammable surface at least 3 feet from anything combustible, away from foot traffic (HGTV).
